content.text:
I went down a bit of a meteorite rabbit hole today. I saw a video where somebody was showing and explaining their meteorite and I couldn't help but wonder how far and how long the asteroid had traveled. I've always been fascinated when thinking about the state of things in the far past. Looking at a meteorite, you are journeying vast distances and peering into the far past. And how long did the asteroid take to get here? Perhaps men lived their entire lives, perhaps civilizations rose and fell, perhaps life itself began during the journey of that little piece of rock from far away in the galaxy to your hand.

Anyways, the net effect was that I am now sure I want a piece of meteorite around. I began searching for meteorite fragments for sale and I quickly realized that these things are not cheap. I ruled out buying one from a traditional vendor; however, I stumbled upon a story of somebody finding one while metal detecting for coins. Thus began my metal detecting rabbit hole. I'll spare the details but I ended up buying a Nokta Simplex Ultra , a DR.ÖTEK pinpointer, and a GQ GMC-800 Geiger Counter. While I have no intention of looking for radioactive things, I've heard many stories of people in my area (Los Alamos, NM) finding spicy things lying around, so I figured I'd rather be safe than irradiated.

content.caption: A short attempt at playing "Big Black Car" by Gregory Alan Isakov

content.text: After ordering all of my metal decting gear, I spent the rest of my day looking at google maps for places to go hike and survey. Part of my decision to try this hobby was also as a means to get some time out in nature moving my body and breathing fresh air. I also played my acoustic for the first time in awhile today after listening to "Big Black Car" by Gregory Alan Isakov. Between grad school applications, work, school, and the holidays, I have not been able to play much recently so it was really nice to sit down and just play for a bit.
